title: Data-classification driven RBAC and audit enrichment shim
author: Priya Khandelwal
release_notes: Add classification-driven RBAC predicates and audit enrichment. New KMS key selector honors classification and region pinning. Rollout gated by feature flag; no immediate breaking changes. Backwards-compatible shim included.
body: Summary: Introduce a classification-aware enforcement shim that carries data-classification labels from ingress through policy evaluation and audit enrichment, and influences KMS key selection. Motivation: customers in regulated industries require per-object handling guarantees (e.g., 'restricted' vs 'public'); prior work enforced tenant+region constraints but lacked classification-aware access controls. This PR implements a light-weight, opt-in path that ties classification to RBAC v2 predicates, audit metadata, and CMK selection.||What this changes: 1) frontproxy now accepts/normalizes X-Data-Classification and validation metadata; 2) a classification predicate for the RBAC v2 evaluator (policy DSL extension) that supports allow/deny by classification and legal_basis; 3) audit pipeline enrichment includes classification, classifier_version and legal_basis with an append-only envelope; 4) KMS allocator update to prefer classification-bound keys and respect region pinning when classification requires residency; 5) a migration shim for older tenants (falls back to preexisting behavior) and an operator-facing rollout flag; 6) new unit/integration/e2e tests and docs.||Design notes: Policies are evaluated after tenant/role checks but before side-effecting operations; classification is treated as an attribute (subject/resource) available to predicates. We keep the shim opt-in via feature.guard.classification_rbac (default: off); when disabled the system behavior is unchanged. KMS selection uses a soft-preference model: if a classification-mapped key exists in the requested region it is selected, otherwise we fall back to tenant-default key and emit an audit flag for operator review.||Testing and rollout: Added exhaustive unit tests around the predicate evaluator, integration tests that assert audit enrichment and KMS selection in multi-region scenarios, and an e2e that simulates cross-border datasets. Canary rollout plan: enable for internal customers, monitor audit volume and false-positive access denials, then progressively enable for opt-in tenants. Rollback: flip feature.guard.classification_rbac to false, which removes predicate enforcement but preserves enriched audit logs.||Commits: See commits list below.||Files changed summary: policy engine + predicate, gateway middleware, audit enricher, kms allocator, helm values, docs, and tests.||Operational considerations: We publish a short migration runbook (docs/compliance/classification-guidelines.md) and a monitoring dashboard with the top N denied requests by classification. Expected performance impact: negligible for common paths (classification header parse + predicate check ~ sub-ms); KMS allocator adds a small consistent lookup (cached).||Security review: encryption of the classification header is recommended for external clients; we added validators and size limits to avoid header injection.||Related: ENG-4821 (classification policy framework), SEC-314 (compliance gating), SUP-8901 (customer support case driving scope)
commits: feat(gateway): accept and validate X-Data-Classification header
feat(policy): add classification predicate to RBAC v2 evaluator
chore(audit): append classification and classifier_version fields to audit envelope
feat(kms): classification-aware key selector with region preference
test: add unit/integration/e2e tests for classification flows
docs: add classification rollout and runbook
review_comments: Lukas Meyer: Please add a unit test for the 'unknown' classification fallback path to ensure we don't accidentally allow restricted data through. Also can we log mismatch reasons at DEBUG level rather than INFO?
Priya Khandelwal (author): Added unknown-classification test and moved mismatch logs to DEBUG (see tests/unit/policy/classification_predicate_test.go and classification_mw.go).
Diya Shah: Audit enrichment looks good, but we should redact classifier_version for public data in the audit UI. Filing a follow-up ticket to add a redaction view for the console.
Marcus Hale: CI flaked on the first integration run; reran pipeline and LGTM. Approving to allow squash-merge with the stated rollback plan.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky on first run; rerun ok)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main after 2 approvals. Commit message consolidated. Rollout will be toggled via feature.guard.classification_rbac; operators notified in #ops-compliance. Post-merge follow-ups: UI audit-redaction ticket and small telemetry tweak to surface denied-by-classification counts.
notes: Backwards compatible: header is optional and shim is opt-in
Operators: ensure helm values.classification.enabled=false until ready
Support: include classifier_version and legal_basis in customer tickets to accelerate triage
